gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Minn Kota tells owners of its brushed (non-QUEST) motors to keep the motor at 85% speed (Speed 8.5) or lower on lithium. Its reason is that LiFePO4 holds a higher voltage that can be "too powerful" for motors built for flooded lead-acid, and running at full speed "can result in damage." Its QUEST motors are the ones it calls "optimized for use with LiFePO4."
standout_why: I opened the cited Ionic trolling-motor category page and three of the top results: TrollCove, which is specifically about Minn Kota, plus Florida Fishing Kayaks and MinorMania. None of them mentions brushed motors, a speed cap, or lithium voltage harming a motor built for lead-acid. MinorMania only refers vaguely to 'older forum threads' about voltage spikes. The Ionic page already says the BMS continuous rating must cover the motor's max amp draw (its example is a 112 lb, 36 V motor drawing 52 A), and Florida Fishing Kayaks and MinorMania already cover the 14.4–14.6 V lithium charge profile, so those points are not new. Wired2Fish, the other cited page, returned HTTP 403, so I could not check it.
decides: This settles whether the plan works without losing anything. On a QUEST-series Minn Kota, any LiFePO4 pack whose BMS continuous rating covers the motor's draw is a straight drop-in. On a brushed Minn Kota (Endura, Traxxis, older Terrova or Ultrex), Minn Kota's own help center says to cap the motor at 85% speed, so the shopper gives up top speed. That makes cheap 100A-BMS packs such as LiTime and Redodo the sensible buy over the $795–$849 premium batteries, because the extra output can't be used. A second check from the same article: if the boat has a Minn Kota PCL on-board charger, its 14.5 V maximum must fall within the battery maker's charge spec.

findings.label: Minn Kota brushed motors on lithium: speed limit
findings.source_title: Lithium Battery Selection and Recommendations (Minn Kota Help Center)
findings.note: Exact quote: "it's recommended to limit the motor speed to 85%, or Speed 8.5 or lower." Also: "Running the motor at maximum speed with lithium batteries can result in damage." The reason given is that lithium holds a higher voltage for longer, which can be "too powerful for motors designed specifically for flooded lead-acid batteries." The article says this applies to brushed motors and contrasts them with QUEST motors. Article last updated 2026-01-14.

findings.label: What happens if the battery's continuous rating is below the motor's max draw
findings.value: The BMS "will restrict power to the motor", which can cause shut-offs, erratic running, and i-Pilot/Spot-Lock problems
findings.source_title: Lithium Battery Selection and Recommendations (Minn Kota Help Center)
findings.note: Minn Kota says to make sure the batteries "provide enough continuous discharge amperage to run the motor at its max amp draw." Its per-thrust chart is only an image (RequiredContinuousDischargeAmperage.png) that I could not read.
